statusNote: Nonprofit (Southern Baptist-affiliated) through 2004; sold to investor group and converted to for-profit (Grand Canyon Education, Inc., publicly traded) in 2004; converted back to nonprofit status in 2018, formally recognized by the U.S. Department of Education in December 2025. Brian Mueller has been CEO of the for-profit services company Grand Canyon Education throughout, and separately holds the title President of the (nonprofit) University.

leaders.notes: Served 22 years as president; stepped down and was elected to a newly created chancellor role effective January 1, 2000, while Gil Stafford became president the same day.

Elected president effective January 1, 2000, at age 46, as Bill Williams moved to the new chancellor post. Resigned January 5, 2004, amid the university's financial crisis to enter the Episcopal priesthood; the university was sold to an investor group later that year.

Not formally titled 'President' -- led GCU as Chief Executive Officer after his investor group (Significant Education LLC) acquired the near-bankrupt, nonprofit GCU in 2004 and converted it to for-profit status; the university reportedly searched for a new president during this period, filled by Kathleen Player in 2008. Included here as the de facto top executive during a gap in the formal presidency; flagged isInterim given the unusual title.

leaders.nextRole: Chief Academic Officer / VP of Health Sciences (remained at GCU)
leaders.notes: Joined GCU in 1998, rose through dean and provost roles, and was named President of the University on August 1, 2008 (around the same time Brian Mueller became CEO of the newly formed public parent company). Ceded the University president title to Mueller around 2012 and continued in an academic-officer capacity at GCU.

leaders.priorInstitution: Apollo Education Group, Inc. (parent of University of Phoenix)
leaders.notes: Joined GCU/Grand Canyon Education as CEO on July 1, 2008 and added the University President title around 2012 (re-affirmed July 1, 2018 after GCU's conversion back to nonprofit status). Previously spent two decades at University of Phoenix / Apollo Education Group, where enrollment grew from 3,500 to 340,000 under his watch. Currently sitting president.

leaders.nextRole: President Emeritus (remained affiliated with GVSU, incl. Johnson Center for Philanthropy Leadership Council)
leaders.notes: Became GVSU president in 1969 at age 37 and retired in 2001 as the longest-serving public university president in the country at the time (32 years), overseeing its growth from a small liberal-arts college into a regional university.

leaders.priorTitle: State Treasurer / Education Policy Advisor to Governor John Engler
leaders.notes: Became GVSU's third president July 1, 2001, coming from Michigan state government (state treasurer, state budget director). Left in 2006 to become president of retail chain Meijer, Inc.

leaders.priorInstitution: State University of New York (SUNY) Cobleskill
leaders.nextRole: President Emeritus / faculty (chemistry), remained at GVSU
leaders.notes: Became GVSU's fourth president in July 2006. During his tenure enrollment rose to nearly 25,000 and 2.3 million square feet of facilities were added. Retired June 30, 2019, announced in 2018, and later returned to teach chemistry as a GVSU faculty member.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President and CEO, Lifelong Learning Network (previously Global Network)
leaders.notes: Appointed GVSU's fifth president (and first woman president) by unanimous board vote January 22, 2019, effective July 2019, after 18 years in senior enrollment/global-network leadership roles at Northeastern University. Currently sitting president.

Led Gwynedd-Mercy College (then still a religious-order-led institution) from 1993 to 2002, immediately before the school's first lay president. Went on to serve as president of Barry University, another Catholic institution, from 2004 to 2019.

Gwynedd Mercy's longest-tenured president and its first lay (non-religious-order) president, serving 2002 to her retirement in August 2017 (announced in 2016). Oversaw the college-to-university transition and major campus expansion; also served on the NCAA Division III Presidents' Council.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Became Gwynedd Mercy's sixth president August 1, 2017, after 19+ years in academic leadership roles at two other Mercy-sponsored institutions (Mount Aloysius College and Carlow University). A licensed attorney by training. Currently sitting president.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President of Administrative Services (also previously VP of Student Affairs)
leaders.notes: Became Hampton's 12th president in 1978 and served 44 years, the longest tenure in the university's history, before retiring June 30, 2022. Legacy includes over 90 new academic degrees, a dozen doctoral programs, 29 new buildings, and growing the endowment from $29 million to over $300 million. Also a prominent Pepsi-Cola franchise owner and philanthropist.

Hampton's 13th president since July 1, 2022. A 1983 Hampton graduate (ROTC), he retired from the U.S. Army in 2020 after 37 years and multiple senior military leadership posts before returning to lead his alma mater. He and his wife, Myra Richardson Williams, are the first Hampton president and first lady to both hold Hampton degrees.
